To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

post-error slowing is implemented through the recruitment of a neural network that includes the right dorsolatera prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), the right inferior frontal gyrus (IFG), and the right superior prefrontal cortex.

post-error slowing and increased accuracy are associated with a theta-beta EEG oscillation that is correlated with the activity of the dorsolateral pre-frontal cortex, the inferior frontal cortex, the superior frontal cortex, and with the stop-signal network.

post-error slowing in correct responses after an erroneous trial was related to an increase in the theta-beta component of the EEG, and that post-error caution in the trial following an error was associated with increased activation of right prefrontal and superior frontal regions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neurophysiological mechanisms underlying the adaptation of cognitive processes after an error.
the mechanisms underlying the adaptation of cognitive functions.
the neural mechanisms that underlie cognitive control and the adaptation of behavior after the commission of errors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the increase in control after errors is implemented through a mechanism of inhibition that involves a network of frontal brain regions.

the post-error slowing and post-error caution are two different phenomena, which are both related to an increase of cognitive control, but that the underlying mechanisms are different, the former related to the inhibition of the response and the latter to the inhibition of action.
the increase in control after an error is implemented by the recruitment of an inhibitory neural network that is activated by the need of stopping motor actions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neural mechanisms underlying the adaptation to errors are related to the increase in cognitive inhibition.
the post-error slowing is mediated through a theta-beta oscillatory activity in the prefrontal cortex that is related to the recruitment of an inhibitory network in the right prefrontal cortex.
the brain uses the theta-beta oscillation to control the degree of post-slowing and the right prefrontal cortex to control the degree in caution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
post-error slowing and the increase of caution in the trial after an error are mediated by a common neural mechanism.
the neural mechanisms underlying post-error slowing and the increase in accuracy after the commission of errors involve the activation of the right dorsomedial prefrontal cortex.
the adaptive response following the commission of errors is mediated by a network that includes the right dorsolatera prefrontal cortex and the right inferior frontal gyrus.
